chunks: And through it, from Abdullah ibn Jubla, from Salama ibn Janah, from Hazim ibn Habeeb, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said to him: May God improve you, my parents died and did not perform Hajj, and God has granted me wealth and prosperity, so what do you say about performing Hajj on their behalf? He said: Do it, for it will cool (benefit) them. Then he said to me: O Hazim, the master of this matter has two occultations, and he will appear after the second one. Whoever comes to you saying that he has shaken the dust from his grave (i.e., died), do not believe him.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj for deceased parents and what are the signs of the Imam's occultation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates performing Hajj for deceased parents, noting its spiritual benefit in cooling their chests, while simultaneously linking this personal jurisprudence to the broader eschatological narrative of the Mahdi. He specifically warns against false claimants who assert the Imam's death during the occultation, emphasizing the continuity of his life and authority. This hadith serves as a critical proof for the Shia doctrine of the Mahdi's prolonged life and dual occultations (Sughra and Kubra).
